samples.summary: Delta reverts the CLI login flow's callback-to-flow binding, and deletes the design-doc rationale, without recording the decision or a follow-up
samples.evidence: This delta removes the nonce end-to-end: the CLI no longer mints/echoes a value (`startCallbackServer()` now takes no argument and accepts the first `code` that reaches `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`, login.ts:168-226), the backend no longer stores or echoes it (cli-auth.store.ts, github-auth.guard.ts, auth.controller.ts), and the paragraphs in docs/design/cli.md §3.1 and docs/design/rest-api.md §7 that documented *why* the binding existed (RFC 8252 §8.9 — guessable loopback port, any page in the browser can push a code) are deleted rather than replaced with an accepted-risk / Non-Goal / follow-up note. The docs now describe a loopback OAuth callback with no `state` at all, while docs/design/rest-api.md:367 still claims "OAuth state forgery (CSRF)" is mitigated by a token "validated on callback" — and the only remaining state material, `CliAuthStore`'s `csrf`, is never compared anywhere (grep for `csrf` finds no consumer outside the store and its spec). If the removal is a deliberate descope, the design docs are the place it has to be written down; as it stands the PR silently walks back a documented design property.
searchedFor: grep -i nonce across repo (only unrelated hits)

samples.summary: Risk table still claims the CLI OAuth state/CSRF token is "validated on callback", which no code does after this revert
samples.evidence: rest-api.md:367 keeps the row "OAuth state forgery (CSRF) | Backend generates a random 32-byte CSRF token per OAuth request, stores in a 5-minute in-memory map, and validates on callback." The delta edits §7 two paragraphs above it but leaves this row; `consumeState` returns `csrf` and no caller compares it (auth.controller.ts:120-135 reads only `mode`/`port`). With the nonce gone this is the only binding claim left in the docs and it is not implemented, so the doc overstates the shipped design.

samples.evidence: The revised §9 narrows the rule to "Every emitter on the data path" and names `login` and `ctx switch` as exceptions "tracked in #654/#655". The prose-error sites are real and only these two (login.ts:63,80,97; ctx.ts:61,67), so the claim is accurate, but weakening a stated output convention in the design doc rather than in code means the doc now documents a divergence it previously forbade; if those two are genuinely out of scope, a Non-Goals entry would be the cleaner home than a mid-convention parenthetical.

The docs now describe a loopback OAuth callback with no `state` at all, while docs/design/rest-api.md:367 still claims "OAuth state forgery (CSRF)" is mitigated by a token "validated on callback" — and the only remaining state material, `CliAuthStore`'s `csrf`, is never compared anywhere (grep for `csrf` finds no consumer outside the store and its spec). searchedFor: grep -i nonce across repo (only unrelated hits)

verdict.reason: The claimed state is present in the tree. The CLI callback server takes no per-flow value and accepts the first `code` delivered to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback (login.ts:33, 153-182), and the backend echoes only `code` back to the loopback URL (auth.controller.ts:120-128; github-auth.guard.ts:19-24), so no callback-to-flow binding exists. The only remaining state material, `CliAuthStore`'s `csrf` (cli-auth.store.ts:5,25,34,46), has no consumer anywhere outside the store and its spec. The design docs neither document the property nor record its removal: cli.md §3.1 (168-198) describes the loopback callback with no state/nonce and no accepted-risk note, cli.md Non-Goals (55-68) has no such descope entry, and 'RFC 8252'/'loopback' appear nowhere under docs/ — while rest-api.md:367 still claims OAuth state forgery is mitigated by a CSRF token 'validated on callback'. That is a live design-doc-discipline/spec-conformance mismatch (docs contradict implementation, undocumented walk-back), which is in this lens's lane. No guard makes it moot and nothing refutes it, so it stands.

finding.summary: Two unrelated changes bundled in one PR: an OAuth loopback-binding (nonce/state) security fix across backend+CLI, and the #661 error-envelope `command` attribution refactor touching ~20 CLI files. Neither depends on the other, and the design docs for each land in different sections (cli.md "Login flow" / rest-api.md "CLI Auth" vs cli.md §9). If the originating issue is #661 (as every test comment cites), the auth change is unrequested scope; if it is the auth issue, the envelope refactor is. Splitting would let each be reviewed and reverted independently.
finding.evidence: login.ts adds nonce minting; formatter.ts adds errorEnvelope/backendErrorEnvelope; test comments cite "#661" only for the envelope work.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the PR bundles an added "OAuth loopback-binding (nonce/state) security fix across backend+CLI" alongside the #661 error-envelope refactor, citing nonce minting in login.ts. The envelope half is real (formatter.ts exports errorEnvelope:75, backendErrorEnvelope:118, outputError:156, per the #661 todo doc), but the auth half does not exist as described. I read all 271 lines of packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts: the OAuth URL is `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}` (line 36) with no nonce and no state, and the callback handler reads only `code` (line 177) with no binding comparison. A repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `nonce` yields zero source hits (only en_US.dic, pnpm-lock.yaml, a design-editor sandbox doc, and other reviewers' .agent-review artifacts). The backend CLI-auth state/CSRF store that does exist (cli-auth.store.ts, github-auth.guard.ts:24 createState, auth.controller.ts:120 consumeState) is pre-existing shipped design, documented in docs/design/rest-api.md §7 (lines 328-342, 367) and docs/design/cli.md §3.1 (lines 168-198) and implemented by the archived 2026-03-15 CLI OAuth login task (Chunk 1 Task 2, marked complete). There is therefore no separable added auth feature in the tree to split out, so the bundling premise fails at its cited location. (The tree in fact shows an *unbound* loopback callback, which is a correctness/security concern owned by those lenses and reported there, not the design-fit scope-creep claim made here.)

finding.summary: docs/design/cli.md §9 now asserts "Every emitter builds it through `errorEnvelope` / `backendErrorEnvelope` … so 'one line, attributed' holds", but several CLI error paths still emit bare, unstructured text and bypass the envelope entirely: `login` (`console.error('Token exchange failed…')` L73, `'Failed to fetch user info.'` L90, `Failed to fetch workspaces…` L107, each followed by `process.exit(1)`) and `ctx switch` (`'Not logged in…'` L61, `Workspace not found: …` L67). The doc's universal claim is therefore not satisfied by the implementation — either narrow the claim to the enumerated paths or convert these emitters too.
finding.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:73,90,107; packages/cli/src/commands/ctx.ts:61,67 emit plain strings, not JSON envelopes.

verdict.reason: The finding rests on docs/design/cli.md §9 making a universal claim that every CLI error path uses the envelope. It does not. The sentence at cli.md:1023-1031 scopes the claim to "Every emitter on the data path" and then to "the paths that never throw either", enumerating them (import/upload/download orchestrators, docs/notes/slides backend-error passthroughs, schema lookup miss), and immediately adds: "The exceptions are the two interactive session commands, `login` and `ctx switch`, which still print prose to a human at a terminal rather than an envelope to an agent (tracked in #654/#655)". The two commands the finding cites are named as explicit, tracked exceptions. The reviewer's quoted evidence truncates the sentence at "holds", omitting the narrowing clause and the exception carve-out. The bare emitters themselves do exist (login.ts:63-66, 80-81, 97-100; ctx.ts:61-63, 67-69 — line numbers shifted ~10 from the finding), but the doc already documents them as exceptions, which is precisely the remedy the finding requests ("narrow the claim to the enumerated paths"). No spec/doc mismatch remains under the design-fit rubric.

finding.summary: Scope creep: the PR converts the hand-rolled error emitters the issue's own task plan explicitly deferred. The plan's Scope note (lines 19–22) says the forwarded upstream bodies in `docs.ts`/`slides.ts`/`notes.ts`, `src/docs/import.ts`, `src/files/*` and `schema.ts` "are the subject of #654/#655 and are left alone here", yet this diff rewrites every one of them through the new `backendErrorEnvelope`/`errorEnvelope` builders (packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:202, notes.ts:155, slides.ts:161, schema.ts:40, files/upload.ts, files/download.ts, docs/import.ts, notes/import.ts, slides/import.ts). Either the scope note should be updated in this PR (it was not) or the work belongs in #654/#655, where it now risks duplicating/conflicting with in-flight work. The #661 acceptance criteria (single line, `command`, unchanged code/message) are satisfied by the `outputError` change alone.
finding.evidence: todo.md:19-22 "Scope note: … Hand-rolled emitters that bypass `outputError` (…) are the subject of #654/#655 and are left alone here." vs. diff converting all of them.

verdict.reason: The finding's cited evidence does not exist. docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:19-29 contains a revised scope note stating the opposite of the quoted text: "Scope note (revised while implementing): the original note deferred every emitter that bypasses outputError. That does not survive contact with the acceptance criteria — the emitters that forward a backend error body (docs.ts/slides.ts/notes.ts, src/docs/import.ts, src/notes/import.ts, src/slides/import.ts, src/files/*, schema.ts) … They are converted here through a shared backendErrorEnvelope. What stays deferred to #654/#655 is the interactive prose in login and ctx switch." A grep for "left alone here" across docs/ returns no hits. The plan step at lines 43-45 explicitly lists routing the backend-body emitters through the shared builders, and the canonical design doc docs/design/cli.md:1017-1038 was updated to match, naming the converted paths and listing login/ctx switch as the only #654/#655 exceptions. The code agrees: formatter.ts:75-140 defines the shared errorEnvelope/backendErrorEnvelope with that rationale, and login.ts still emits prose (console.error at 37-38, 80, 97), so the deferred set really is still deferred. The claim that the scope note defers this work and "was not" updated is therefore not present as described.

finding.summary: No task plan under `docs/tasks/active/` for the OAuth nonce work. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 requires a feature / non-trivial change to have both an updated design doc *and* a task plan (`YYYYMMDD-<slug>-todo.md` with a paired `-lessons.md`). The design docs (cli.md login flow, rest-api.md CLI Auth) were updated, but no todo/lessons pair exists for the nonce change; the only active CLI task doc is the #661 envelope one, whose plan does not mention login at all.
finding.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 'Feature / non-trivial change → write or update a design doc … → create a task plan under docs/tasks/active/'.

verdict.reason: The finding's premise is not present in the repository. It claims the change contains OAuth "nonce" work documented in docs/design/cli.md's login flow and rest-api.md's CLI Auth section, and that a task plan for it is missing. But a repo-wide case-insensitive grep for `nonce` matches only docs/design/design-editor/design-editor-sandbox-recipe.md, packages/docs/src/spell/dict/en_US.dic and pnpm-lock.yaml — nothing in the CLI, backend auth, or any design doc. Concretely: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts has zero occurrences of `state`/`nonce` (the loopback handler reads only `code`); github-auth.guard.ts:16-31 only range-checks the port and takes `{ stateToken }`; auth.controller.ts:127-129 redirects with `?code=` only, with no `&state=` echo; docs/design/cli.md:168-198 and docs/design/rest-api.md:328-353 describe the pre-existing CSRF-state-token/port-validation design with no nonce or state echo (grep for `state=|state echo|RFC 8252` in docs/design/ matches nothing in either file). The correctness lens' own record for this same delta states it "reverts the nonce/`state` echo end to end", matching what the tree shows. There is therefore no nonce feature in this change that CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 / :60-63 would require a task plan for. Separately, the work that IS in this delta (#661 error envelope) does have the required pair: docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md (issue #661, plan + acceptance criteria, with login prose explicitly deferred to #654/#655 at line 27) and its paired -lessons.md. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 quoted by the reviewer is accurate, but the change it is applied to contains no nonce/architecture work to document.
